candidates.observed_friction: The real distutils builder/reviewer exchange is split across a task board, review prose, a patch and a response record; compatibility with the existing shared artifact schema is unknown.
candidates.potential_agent_value: A schema-valid handoff could expose reviewer findings and builder disposition to another agent without a new coordinator.
candidates.cheapest_falsifying_test: Represent the completed exchange with the existing schema, validate it, and compare four decision-critical facts with the source records.
candidates.simpler_alternative: Keep the existing Markdown board if the schema needs expansion for this single exchange.
candidates.cost: One small JSON fixture, existing validation path or a direct schema check, and normal LAB reporting.

candidates.observed_friction: The compact-success practice has only one recorded consumer.
candidates.potential_agent_value: Reduce success-only verification output while retaining diagnosis on failure.
candidates.cheapest_falsifying_test: Use the next independent consumer or natural failing run.
candidates.simpler_alternative: Retain the existing shell practice; this session is not an independent consumer and should not manufacture failure.
candidates.cost: No discriminating comparison is currently available.

candidates.observed_friction: Two old opus branches appear unmerged by ancestry.
candidates.evidence: The startup branch audit classified both commits as patch-equivalent with git cherry '-'.
candidates.potential_agent_value: Avoid treating squash/rebase-equivalent branches as unfinished work.
candidates.cheapest_falsifying_test: Use native merged/no-merged plus git cherry, already completed at startup.
candidates.simpler_alternative: Keep the native command; build no wrapper.
candidates.cost: The observed workflow already resolved the ambiguity, so further work has no incremental value.

real_task: Determine whether the existing agent artifact schema can carry the completed builder/reviewer handoff for distutils #433.
observed_problem: A downstream agent currently has to correlate several files to learn the review findings, revised artifact, builder disposition and next approval boundary.
baseline: No schema-valid artifact has yet represented this real builder/reviewer exchange; the four decision-critical facts are available only by correlating its source records.
hypothesis: One instance using the existing schema can preserve all four facts without changing the schema or adding a coordinator.
minimum_useful_effect: 4/4 facts represented, schema validation passes, and no source contradiction is introduced.
quality_control: Validate against the tracked schema, then manually cross-check role attribution, reviewer findings, builder disposition and human-review boundary against the Session 113-114 records.
overhead: Include mandatory startup, source reading, fixture construction, validation, reporting, tests, checkpoint and publication.
stop_condition: Do not expand the schema or build orchestration from one example. If the existing contract cannot represent all four facts, record the gap and retain the Markdown board.

result.finding: The existing adoption artifact can preserve role attribution, reviewer findings, builder disposition and the human-review boundary, but those details remain prose rather than separately queryable fields.

decision_reason: Keep one schema-valid real example and make it discoverable from the protocol. Do not expand the schema or add coordination software until another consumer needs structured routing or prose loses a decision-critical fact.
agent_interaction: Agent 2's adversarial findings and Agent 1's acceptance were combined into the existing public adoption-artifact contract.
limitations: This is a replay of one completed exchange, not a field comparison or evidence that agents consume the artifact more effectively than the Markdown board. Validation required an ephemeral six-package jsonschema environment.
